scope: src/ (whole project; no scope was specified)

findings.title: Sorting and filtering ~50,000 rows on every keystroke
findings.explanation: A comment states `players` always holds about 50,000 rows. The component copies and sorts the whole array and then filters it during render. The `query` state changes on every keystroke, so each keystroke re-runs an O(n log n) sort and an O(n) filter. The sort does not depend on `query`, so that work is wasted. This blocks the main thread and makes typing in the search box laggy.
findings.evidence:
const ranked = [...players].sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score);
  const visible = ranked.filter((p) => p.name.includes(query)).slice(0, 20);
findings.suggested_fix: Compute `ranked` once with `useMemo(() => [...players].sort(...), [players])`, or sort before passing the data in or on the server. Also consider `useDeferredValue(query)` for the filter, or server-side search and pagination so the client does not hold 50k rows.

findings.title: Array index used as key on a removable list of uncontrolled inputs
findings.explanation: Todos can be removed through `onRemove`, and each row holds an uncontrolled `<input defaultValue>` whose typed text lives in the DOM. With `key={i}`, removing a middle item makes React reuse the DOM nodes by position. `defaultValue` is only read on mount, so the remaining rows keep the previous row's edited text and show the wrong content next to the wrong Remove button.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the stable id: `<li key={t.id}>`. The index can stay in the aria-label.
